name: Premium Dog Food Market
description: Size the market for a premium dog food brand.
formula: TAM = Population x Penetration_rate x Purchase_frequency x Average_spend
solution_logic: Step 1: Identify addressable population = target_population x addressable_segment
Step 2: Apply penetration rate = addressable_population x penetration_rate
Step 3: Calculate annual spend per user = purchase_frequency x avg_spend_per_purchase
Step 4: Calculate TAM = penetrating_users x annual_spend_per_user
key_insight: Market sizing is about defensible assumptions, not precision. Show your logic clearly -- the interviewer is testing your structure, not your arithmetic.
common_mistakes: Sizing the total population instead of the addressable segment
Forgetting purchase frequency -- confusing annual vs per-transaction spend
Not sanity-checking the output against known benchmarks
framework_soundbite: Top-down or bottom-up -- pick one, state your assumptions, and sanity-check the output. The logic matters more than the number.
business_contexts: a direct-to-consumer premium dog food startup
a pet CPG brand considering a premium line extension
question_patterns: A private-equity firm is evaluating an investment in a premium dog food brand and wants to understand the total market opportunity before committing to diligence.

prompts.beginner: Estimate the total addressable market for premium dog food in the United States.
prompts.intermediate: A private-equity firm is evaluating an investment in a premium dog food brand and wants to understand the total market opportunity before committing to diligence.
prompts.advanced: A mid-market PE firm has been approached by a founder-led premium dog food company seeking growth capital. The founder's own materials are vague about geographic scope and what counts as a "premium" customer. Before committing further diligence resources, the investment team wants a defensible view of market size.
